nodes.label: Locator tiers (resolver order)
nodes.rationale: Four tiers ordered by robustness vs precision: role+accessible name survives cosmetic change but needs ARIA; text/label is robust but breaks on copy changes; stable attrs are precise but most brittle; structural relations are last resort. A tier wins by resolving to exactly one element - there is deliberately no scoring and no cache, contrary to what the failure taxonomy describes.

nodes.label: near: document-order proximity
nodes.rationale: Six load-bearing rules, each bought with a red case: document order not pixels (a HN subline's bounding box contains every link so geometric distance ties at 0); the anchor is not its own neighbour; but a candidate wrapping the anchor beats every neighbour; match the anchor exactly before substring; refuse rather than tie-break; not a relocation rung but rungs must carry it forward.

nodes.label: Fixture map
nodes.rationale: All fixtures are served by the same FastAPI app (GET /fixtures/{name}) so eval and production share one serving path.

nodes.label: ?mut= deterministic HTML mutations
nodes.rationale: B-floor mutations each break exactly one locator tier - that is the point, so surviving is evidence of relocating rather than of luck.

nodes.label: A fixture must survive its own mutations
nodes.rationale: ids-renamed renames every id/for/data-testid, so fixture scripts must resolve their own elements by tag/aria-label; otherwise the mutation breaks the page instead of the agent's stable-attr dependency and the L4 case measures nothing (learned via l4-shop-ids-renamed, guarded by mutation-catalog-integrity).
nodes.norm_label: a fixture must survive its own mutations

nodes.label: Addressable ARIA roles (Playwright 1.49)
nodes.rationale: ARIA prohibits an author name on definition/term/code/emphasis/strong/caption/time, so Chromium's snapshot shows a name get_by_role(name=) will never match; observe() blanks those names for exactly that reason.

nodes.label: Postcondition patterns (expected_state)
nodes.rationale: The executor records postcondition_ok: null and carries on; the verifier is what fails the run for an unverified state-changing step, so grading never depends on the executor's own conclusion.

nodes.label: Playwright pitfalls
nodes.rationale: a11y snapshot over raw DOM dumps (token budget); never sleep, always assert the postcondition; strict-mode violations are locate/ambiguous not an excuse for .first(); bot-block pages are env + stop, never evade.

nodes.label: agent.FILLABLE_JS fillability predicate
nodes.rationale: Locator.is_editable() means 'enabled and not readonly' and returns True for a <button> in 1.49, so it cannot answer whether an element can hold a value; without an explicit tag/type check a fill onto the wrong element reports act for a locate root cause.

nodes.label: OpenRouter planner calls + budget counter
nodes.rationale: Planner default anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5, planning/replanning only; every call goes through the budget counter and is stubbed at the module boundary in the fast suite so the offline gate costs $0.00.

nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md - the facts layer, kept short on purpose.

nodes.label: Eval suite tags: invariant/fast/live/full/all
nodes.rationale: live and full are separate tags on purpose: live is every case needing the network, full adds the ones that also spend LLM tokens, so --suite live exercises real sites at $0.00 while paid cases stay behind full.

nodes.rationale: groundwork targets problems where requirements are clear but correctness is hard to define up front, so correctness is encoded as executable invariants and metrics rather than prose.

nodes.label: Eight hard rules
nodes.rationale: Baseline moves are decisions requiring an ADR; every new failure becomes a case before it is fixed and must be watched red first, because an eval never seen red proves nothing.

nodes.label: Rule 6 - no site-specific knowledge in execution policy
nodes.rationale: Production agent code contains no site-specific selectors, DOM paths or navigation recipes, so 'supporting' a site is never a hardcoding exercise. Eval/fixture code may use them strictly for ground-truth verification and fault injection. Allowed per-site data anywhere: start URL, rate limit, ground-truth API endpoint.

nodes.label: Four layers, no overlap (facts/knowledge/execution/enforcement)
nodes.rationale: The failure mode this prevents is writing enforcement-layer intent into the facts layer, where it becomes a polite suggestion an agent can talk itself past. Advice doesn't bind agents; enforcement does.

nodes.label: Honest failure modes (generated from cases)
nodes.rationale: Every unreliable/unsupported row cites a case id and an invariant-suite case fails if a citation stops resolving, or if the document parses to zero declared limitations - so the limitation list cannot rot.

nodes.label: An eval set is blind where its author was already looking
nodes.source_location: Where AI helped, and where it was wrong
nodes.rationale: 18 defects across six milestones were found by cold review or by adding a new domain - not by the eval suite - in code green at the time. The only two things observed to move the blind spot are adversarial review and unfamiliar input, which is why cold review is a gate rather than a nicety.
nodes.norm_label: an eval set is blind where its author was already looking

nodes.label: Every suite stubs the planner
nodes.rationale: Deliberate under cost-discipline so the offline gate costs $0.00 and runs without a key, but it means measured pass rates grade the resolver-executor-verifier path and say nothing about planning quality.

nodes.label: Cost - $0.0000 measured, two real observed runs
nodes.rationale: A cost-per-task table built on n=2 would be fabrication, so the two runs ($0.0029 and $0.0065) are given as runs. Budgets bound cost rather than measure it; MAX_FIXES is a ceiling never reached because the resolver never generates more than two candidates.
nodes.norm_label: cost - $0.0000 measured, two real observed runs

nodes.label: Runtime performance (bimodal latency)
nodes.rationale: Nearly all latency above the median is SETTLE_TRIES x SETTLE_MS, paid on exactly the cases whose subject is a failing postcondition - the mechanism under test, so it is paid rather than mocked.

nodes.label: Scalability limits (concurrency one, in-memory runs)
nodes.rationale: asyncio.Semaphore(1) serialises execution so a single small instance cannot be pushed into memory exhaustion by concurrent Chromium contexts. RUNS/STREAMS are in-memory and lost on redeploy; the progress stream is single-consumer; rate limiting is per-process, not per-IP.

nodes.label: Trap cases are a floor, not an accuracy
nodes.rationale: Six trap-* cases encode wrong answers that look right and all six are caught, but the traps were written by the same author as the verifier and there is no hand-labeled precision/recall sample, so 6/6 is reported as a detection floor.

nodes.label: Probe #8 - the scope guard was bypassable
nodes.rationale: The regex needed a word boundary after 'in', so 'log into' slipped through; the agent reached a real Google login wall and burned $0.0235, 5x a normal run. The suite never caught it because l5-refuse-login used the spaced form the pattern happened to match - the cases were written to the regex.
nodes.norm_label: probe #8 - the scope guard was bypassable

nodes.label: No check asks whether an answer is responsive
nodes.rationale: Probe #5 returned a 20-book page dump and was rejected on a whitespace technicality in the grounded check, not on relevance. Had the whitespace round-tripped, a page dump would have been reported as a successful answer - the no-fabrication guarantee held by luck.
nodes.norm_label: no check asks whether an answer is responsive

nodes.label: Deployment verified against the live URL
nodes.rationale: Until M5 the instance served the M1 deploy-spike build for four milestones; the gap was invisible from inside the repo, which is why this section exists.
nodes.norm_label: deployment verified against the live url

nodes.label: Seven top-level failure classes
nodes.rationale: nav/locate/act/extract/semantic/env/task. Subclasses are deliberately NOT pre-designed - they accrete through the failure-triage loop, because pre-built taxonomies measure fidelity to our own guesses. Every run's failure carries exactly one top-level class.

nodes.label: Self-correction loop (observe-classify-hypothesize-select-execute-verify)
nodes.rationale: CLASSIFY is deterministic rules over Playwright errors and page state - no LLM in the classifier at B-level. Recovery ladders are evidence-driven, selected by the scope checkpoint from an observed failure distribution, never a third family just to fill a quota.

nodes.label: Retry vs recovery is a trace-level flag
nodes.rationale: Only classify to strategy-switch to verified-success counts toward the recovery metric; 'retry with LLM' is structurally impossible to log as recovery. Conflating correction and maintenance into 'retry' is the failure mode the assignment explicitly grades against.
nodes.norm_label: retry vs recovery is a trace-level flag

nodes.label: Self-maintenance (locator abstraction + relocation loop)
nodes.rationale: Correction = diagnose a failed step and switch strategy; maintenance = detect that a previously working locator no longer matches and relocate the semantic target. Distinct mechanisms with distinct tests.

nodes.label: Locator cache + drift events (designed, not built)
nodes.rationale: The M6 spec-drift audit recorded that three parts of this design are not built: no scoring (no uniqueness x visibility x tier prior), no locator cache, and therefore no drift event - stale detection is just a failed resolve. Written down here rather than quietly diverging.
nodes.norm_label: locator cache + drift events (designed, not built)

nodes.label: Quantified mutation test (one tier at a time)
nodes.rationale: Breaking one locator tier at a time gives controlled, reproducible evidence of 'detect UI change and adjust dynamically' (T4), independent of real sites deciding to change.
nodes.norm_label: quantified mutation test (one tier at a time)

nodes.label: Task 1 A-level plan
nodes.rationale: A-level is not feature count - it is anchored to rubric cell E5 plus the two gaps the B-freeze actually measured: thin live capability, and verifier guarantees that held by luck once.

nodes.label: A-exit criteria (the A-freeze line)
nodes.rationale: Criterion 7 (repo stays private) was struck rather than deleted, because server-side branch protection on main is unavailable on a free plan while private - an exit criterion that quietly disappears is exactly the drift spec-drift exists to catch.

nodes.label: A-phase hour guard (+12h from reopen)
nodes.rationale: The B-phase guard is what made the freeze happen, so the A-phase gets one too: an unbounded reopen is the exact failure the freeze rule existed to prevent.

nodes.label: Report-assisted, human-declared status
nodes.rationale: A pass-rate does not threshold itself into 'supported' - declaring is an engineering-judgment act, and the reason column is the graded honesty evidence. README and the frontend render the same data so the page and the repo cannot disagree.

nodes.label: Declared limitations (each citing a case id)
nodes.norm_label: declared limitations (each citing a case id)

nodes.label: openlibrary.org unreachable since M6 implementation
nodes.rationale: Four committed live runs fail both OL cases failure:nav at page.goto while the other two domains answer normally in the same runs. The agent's behaviour is correct: a site that will not load is a loud failure:nav, not a fabricated answer.

nodes.label: near: degenerates inside shadow DOM
nodes.rationale: Playwright's locators pierce open shadow roots and document.querySelectorAll('*') does not, so every candidate ties and the first wins. Not fixed because a fix with no fixture behind it is how the three near: defects shipped.

nodes.label: A fill into contenteditable is failed act after it worked
nodes.norm_label: a fill into contenteditable is failed act after it worked

nodes.label: Capability is about one hop deep
nodes.rationale: There is no compare/rank/filter step in the plan vocabulary, so 'which is cheapest' is planned as 'extract the whole list'.
nodes.norm_label: capability is about one hop deep

nodes.label: Identity anchors satisfiable on aggregate pages
nodes.rationale: On a listing every candidate entity is in the page text, so the anchor certifies the wrong answer too. The larger of the two anchor holes, and it sits exactly where TC2/TC4 live.
nodes.norm_label: identity anchors satisfiable on aggregate pages

nodes.label: A locator broken at both reachable tiers is not recovered
nodes.rationale: Relocation has exactly two rungs to climb between, role and text. structural became reachable at M6 but only when a plan asks for it, because a rung must be derivable from the failed target's own strings. attrs exists in the taxonomy and in no code path.
nodes.norm_label: a locator broken at both reachable tiers is not recovered

nodes.label: OPENROUTER_API_KEY escalation (live case ships unrun)
nodes.rationale: Extracting a live secret into a local shell and transcript is what CLAUDE.md rule 8 exists to prevent, so the live-planner case ships unrun and declared with two clean paths recorded.

nodes.label: The suite going green is not a review
nodes.rationale: The milestone was judged done when the suite went green and the reviews were proposed as a checklist item; the reviews then found seven things, three of them wrong answers reported as successes and one an over-claim in the author's own prose. Second consecutive milestone where the highest-value defects came from a reader rather than the cases.
nodes.norm_label: the suite going green is not a review

nodes.label: A heuristic whose justification does not survive being written out
nodes.rationale: 'Forward wins, because a label precedes its value more often than it follows' is true of labels; the anchor in a listing query is a value, and the rule confidently returned 'Add to cart' as the product that costs $24.50.
nodes.norm_label: a heuristic whose justification does not survive being written out

nodes.label: RunResult output contract
nodes.rationale: Every run - CLI, gateway, or eval adapter - returns exactly this shape; the eval adapter and the frontend both consume it, so drift here is contract-drift that spec-drift audits field by field.

nodes.label: TraceStep record
nodes.rationale: One record per attempted step; the trace is complete - every action attempted appears in order, no post-hoc reconstruction.

nodes.label: SemanticTarget five-key schema (closed)
nodes.rationale: role/name/text/near/index are the whole schema. A key outside it stops the run as failure:task; it used to be dropped, so the step ran against whatever was left of the target - a plan quietly reinterpreted and a result reported for the weaker task that actually ran.

nodes.label: target.near (proximity, tier structural)
nodes.rationale: Wins as tier structural because proximity is a relation between elements rather than a property of one. Document order, not pixels. Proximity refuses rather than guesses twice over: disjoint anchor matches and equidistant candidates are both loud locate failures.

nodes.label: target.index (k-th match)
nodes.rationale: 'The first search result' is a browsing primitive, not site knowledge. Without it, several matches remain a loud locate failure. near and index answer the same question; when a plan carries both, near decides.

nodes.label: resolved.tier attribution
nodes.rationale: A target carrying near is recorded as structural however its candidates were gathered, because proximity is what identified the element. The self-maintenance metric reads this field. attrs is named because the taxonomy defines the full ladder and no run has ever emitted it.

nodes.label: Identity anchor on extract steps
nodes.rationale: The distinguishing string of the entity the task names; absent from the page the answer was read from means failure:semantic. Two known limits with cases: substring test passes a near-miss entity, and aggregate pages satisfy the anchor with the wrong answer. Only ground truth catches either, and a live run has none.

nodes.label: page_changed (did the action move the page)
nodes.rationale: It exists for one decision: a replan may drop the step it replaces only when that step actually moved the page. Two runs identical in plan, trace and failure differ only in whether the click did anything - nothing about the plan separates them, so the page does. Known ceiling: whole-body text equality.
nodes.norm_label: page_changed (did the action move the page)

nodes.label: superseded_by (a failed attempt stays in the trace)
nodes.rationale: The exemption is gated in the verifier: a supersede pointing at an attempt not in the trace is itself a FAIL, and the last attempt in a chain is never superseded, so its failure always counts.
nodes.norm_label: superseded_by (a failed attempt stays in the trace)

nodes.label: SSE progress stream (step/done events)
nodes.rationale: The stream is the trace, not a highlight reel: a viewer that showed only the steps that worked would render a tidier run than the one that happened, and nothing else in the suite would go red for it.

nodes.label: Invariants bound to the contract (INV-0..INV-3)
nodes.rationale: This document is prose and prose does not fail a build; contract-trace-schema.json is its executable half. Add a field here and the case goes red until the code emits it - which is how anchor was caught, specced and never emitted.

nodes.label: partial status (specced, no code path produces it)
nodes.rationale: Scheduled for M2 with OutcomeVerifier L2 and did not land: nothing in the B-floor task set enumerates a set whose subset is meaningfully correct. Until a case demands it, incomplete enumerations surface as failures, never as quiet successes.
nodes.norm_label: partial status (specced, no code path produces it)

nodes.label: Decision 1 - near: is the structural tier
nodes.rationale: near: had been in the target schema since M1 and in no code path; live breadth made that expensive because on a real site the interesting value usually has no name of its own, only a label beside it. Six properties are load-bearing and each cost a red case; three were written after the first implementation shipped green and was cold-reviewed.
nodes.norm_label: decision 1 - near: is the structural tier

nodes.label: Decision 2 - three silent-wrongness defects fixed at the shared path
nodes.rationale: All three are the same family - the run reports on something other than what it did - and all three are fixed once where every caller routes through, rather than at the site that exposed them. The fillability guard sits in the executor's fill path, not the relocation rung, because a first-attempt plan targeting a non-fillable element is the same defect.
nodes.norm_label: decision 2 - three silent-wrongness defects fixed at the shared path

nodes.label: Decision 3 - hard rule 6 carve-out for stub plans
nodes.rationale: A stub_plan is injected planner output, not execution policy, and rule 6 governs policy. A plan is exactly the artifact allowed to name page-specific things, because a real planner produces one by reading the page. Two conditions keep it honest: no fixture data reaches src/browser/ outside a plan, and every stubbed case measures the resolver/executor/verifier path only. A stub plan encoding a recovery recipe would breach this.
nodes.norm_label: decision 3 - hard rule 6 carve-out for stub plans

nodes.label: Decision 4 - what stays declared rather than fixed
nodes.rationale: Shadow DOM degeneration, contenteditable readback, and inflated rung counts are real, reproducible and deliberately unfixed; none can produce a wrong answer reported as success, and a fix with no fixture behind it is how the first three near defects got here.
nodes.norm_label: decision 4 - what stays declared rather than fixed

nodes.label: Decision 5 - what the M6 numbers license
nodes.rationale: Live cases exist for 3 domains and 3 task classes; only 2 of each are verified green, and the smaller number is the one that counts. Exercising a class, diagnosing it correctly, and supporting it are three different claims.
nodes.norm_label: decision 5 - what the m6 numbers license

nodes.label: shop-lamp-spec.html fixture
nodes.rationale: The only fixture whose rendered text passes agent.PAGE_TEXT_KEEP (2000 chars); lengthening or reordering it silently disarms two cases.

nodes.label: Scope-less <th> label/value spec table
nodes.rationale: The <th> cells deliberately carry no scope attribute - that is how books.toscrape writes them, and it makes Chromium compute role cell for the label as well as the value, so a target naming the label by proximity has to exclude the label's own cell.

nodes.label: Deliberately long description + trailing serial line
nodes.rationale: Real product pages put a wall of copy between the spec table and the footer; evidence-window-keeps-the-anchor depends on the serial line at the bottom sitting outside the stored evidence window.
nodes.norm_label: deliberately long description + trailing serial line

nodes.label: shop-order.html fixture
nodes.rationale: Carries the two page shapes the repo had never had, both from the M6 cold review, both of which made near: report a confident wrong answer.

nodes.label: Subtotal/Shipping/Total table (substring anchor trap)
nodes.rationale: 'Total' is a suffix of 'Subtotal' and get_by_text is a case-insensitive substring match. Labels are <td>, not <th>, on purpose: with <th> the case could pass on a role-computation accident instead of on the anchor rule.

nodes.label: Order line ending in a call to action (equidistance trap)
nodes.rationale: The product link and the CTA link sit one element either side of the price - equidistant. Every real storefront row ends in one of these; shop.html ends at the price and is the reason this went unseen.
nodes.norm_label: order line ending in a call to action (equidistance trap)

nodes.label: Task 1 milestones tracker
nodes.rationale: Milestone-level only (ADR-001); every row names the reviewer evidence it buys against rubric cells E1-E5.

nodes.label: Scope checkpoint (12 observed failures -> 2 recovery families)
nodes.norm_label: scope checkpoint (12 observed failures -> 2 recovery families)

nodes.label: M6 Live breadth & depth (done)
nodes.rationale: 69/69 fast, 18/18 invariant, live 4/6. Live cases for 3 domains and 3 task classes but only 2 domains and 2 classes verified green; near: implemented as the first mechanism to emit the structural tier; three live-found silent-wrongness defects plus four more from the cold review.

nodes.label: B-floor exit criteria (5 of 6 met at freeze)
nodes.rationale: Criterion 2 was partial at the freeze and is 'substantially closed at M6, not fully met'; the table is updated in place rather than re-stated so the freeze's own reading and its correction sit in one place.
nodes.norm_label: b-floor exit criteria (5 of 6 met at freeze)

nodes.label: Reopen - A-phase (2026-08-17)
nodes.rationale: Owner decision: B-baseline accepted, Task 1 reopens for A-level before submission, Task 2 start deferred. Supersedes the freeze rule by explicit instruction; the A-phase carries its own +12h hour guard so the reopen stays bounded.

nodes.label: Cold review of M3+M4 (6 defects in green code)
nodes.norm_label: cold review of m3+m4 (6 defects in green code)
